rationale: Genuine decision differs from the planted control only in recommended_provisional_status, now 'no'; there are no proposed_intervals. All held texts re-hash and all spans match (EO_11537.txt 1a7ed4c0..., EO_12553.txt 6361bdc5...). Identity: EO 11537, 35 FR 9991, signed June 16, 1970, which the API metadata and the 1989 row agree with. I read the whole original. Its single operative command amends Selective Service Regulations sec. 1631.7(a) by inserting a proviso: registrants in I-A/I-A-O who fail to report for a physical examination may be ordered to induction, with the examination given after reporting. It has no term, sunset or savings clause. EO 12553 (Feb. 25, 1986, 51 FR 7237) orders that 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked', and its p. 7241 table (PDF page 13) lists '11537 Amending Selective Service regulations'. There is no exception, partial scope or savings language. That is presidential whole-order revocation, so NO rests on held ACTOR_TEXT, with the 1989 row as corroboration only. Earlier end: EO 11563 (Sept. 26, 1970) re-prescribes sec. 1631.7, citing 11537, and restates the proviso. That may be an earlier overtaking, which the producer correctly leaves open; it could only move the end earlier and does not alter NO. EO 11555 (sec. 1604.52), EO 11586 (Part 1632) and EO 11606 (sec. 1631.5) neither name 11537 nor touch sec. 1631.7, which I confirmed by text search. Revival: the cruden number search returned 0 matches corpus-wide, even though held 11563 and 12553 cite the number, so it is insensitive here. It shows no revival but is not strong negative evidence. The producer's gap statement is literally true, and no history flags exist. Lifecycle gaps remain: the first effective cessation (11563 overtaking vs. 12553), the 12553 effective date, the Proc. 3989 cross-reference (acting text not held), the fate of the regulatory text in 32 CFR, no complete later-source search, and page images not inspected.
